A.explanation: This shows only half a cycle over distance $x$, which would make $x$ equal to $\lambda/2$. P to Q spans a full wavelength.

B.explanation: This shows half a cycle starting negative, but P is a rarefaction where displacement starts at zero and initially moves positive to the right.

C.explanation: This shows a full sine wave starting at zero, going positive then negative, returning to zero at $x$. That matches $x = \lambda$ between successive rarefactions P and Q.

D.explanation: This starts at maximum positive displacement at P, but the centre of a rarefaction has zero displacement, not maximum.

hints: Look at the dot spacing in the diagram: P and Q are both in widely spaced rarefactions with one closely spaced compression about halfway between them.
Recall that for a longitudinal wave the particle displacement $s$ is zero at the centre of a compression and at the centre of a rarefaction, and maximum halfway between them.

Check how many full wavelengths fit between P and Q, and check whether the displacement just to the right of P must be to the right (positive) or to the left (negative) to create the rarefaction at P.
walkthrough: Identify the pattern in the dot diagram. The dots crowd together midway between P and Q, a compression, while P and Q themselves are in spread-out regions, rarefactions.

Successive rarefaction centres are one wavelength apart, so the distance $x$ from P to Q is one full wavelength, $x = \lambda$. The displacement-distance graph must therefore show one complete cycle in distance $x$.
At the exact centre of a rarefaction the displacement is zero, so the graph must start at $0$ at distance $0$ and return to $0$ at distance $x$.
Just to the right of P the particles must have moved away from P to make the spacing wide, i.e. to the right. Taking to the right as positive, the curve must initially go positive from zero.
A sine curve starting at $0$, rising positive then falling through zero to negative and back to zero over one wavelength satisfies all these conditions. This is option C.
